title: How fast does a lethal gene vanish?
hook: Two copies kill, so selection removes it every generation. How long until it is rare?

knows: each person carries two copies of a gene, one from each parent
a hidden (recessive) form shows only with two copies; one-copy carriers look healthy
doesNotKnow: that selection only acts on people with two copies
that a rare harmful copy hides almost entirely in carriers, so removing it gets slower and slower

misconception: A gene that kills in two copies disappears within a few generations.
objective: The learner can explain that in the toy model a copy that kills in two copies falls from 10% to 1% only after 90 generations, because the rarer it gets the more of it sits in healthy carriers that selection cannot see.

claims.text: With random mating, a copy that kills in two copies and does nothing in one changes from share q to q / (1 + q) each generation, so 1/q rises by exactly 1 per generation.
claims.source: Selection against a recessive lethal (Hartl & Clark, Principles of Population Genetics, 2007, ch. 5): q' = q(1-q)/(1-q^2) = q/(1+q); 1/q' = 1/q + 1. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): q/(1+q) from random mating with a recessive lethal; Node.

claims.text: Starting at 10% of copies, it takes 90 generations to fall to 1%; the first 10 generations take it from 10% to 5% and the next 80 take it from 5% to 1%, so each step down is slower. The stage draws this curve.
claims.source: 1/q from 10 to 100 = 90 steps; q(10) = 1/20. Demo.tsx TO_TARGET = 90 and Q[10] = 0.05, iterated; artifacts/scratch/w4life/nums.mjs. Matches the brief's check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: q after 10 generations = 0.0500; after 90 generations = 0.0100.

claims.text: At 10% of copies, 1 baby in 100 is born with two copies and 90% of the bad copies are in healthy carriers; at 1%, 1 in 10,000 and 99%.
claims.source: Hardy-Weinberg at birth: two copies q^2; share of bad copies in carriers 2pq / (2pq + 2q^2) = 1 - q. Shown on the stage at generations 0 and 90. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: q^2 = 0.01 and 0.0001; carrier share of bad copies 1 - q = 0.90 and 0.99.

claims.text: Model: a made-up gene in a large random-mating population, death before breeding with two copies, no effect with one, no new mutations. The stage's 100 people are a rounded picture of the shares.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #36. Stated on the stage before the prediction ('Toy: two bad copies kill before adulthood; one does nothing'). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): The stage message states the toy rules before the prediction.

recall.question: Why does selection against a harmful recessive gene slow down as the gene becomes rare?
options: The gene becomes less harmful over time
Almost all remaining copies sit in healthy carriers, which selection cannot see
Rare genes mutate back to the healthy form
recall.why: Only people with two copies are removed, and when the gene is rare nearly every copy is paired with a healthy one.
